title: GCP Cloud Marketplace Listing Copy Draft — Redwood Inference (SaaS)
content:
DOCUMENT STATUS: Working draft for GCP Cloud Marketplace. Formatting + allowed claims may need adjustment after reviewer feedback.

Owner: Soojin (PMM)
Reviewers needed before submission: Partnerships, Security (Aisha/Marcus), GRC (Olga), Legal (Michael), Finance (Laura), Solutions Engineering (Markus)

====================================================================
1) Proposed listing name (GCP Marketplace)
====================================================================
Redwood Inference — Production LLM Inference (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private)

Alt (shorter): Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM Inference

TODO (Partnerships): confirm final product display name + publisher name constraints in GCP Marketplace.

====================================================================
2) Short description (<= ~200 chars target)
====================================================================
Run and optimize LLM inference with predictable latency, cost controls, and flexible deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or Private/VPC).

Alt: Developer-first LLM inference platform with enterprise procurement via Google Cloud Marketplace.

====================================================================
3) Solution overview / long description (draft)
====================================================================
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Teams use Redwood to ship LLM-powered applications with production-grade performance and operational tooling:
- Low, predictable latency with throughput-optimized serving
- Cost controls (batching/caching guidance, model/quantization recommendations)
- Observability (token-level cost/latency breakdowns, dashboards, tracing hooks)
- Rollouts (canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback policies)
- Enterprise readiness (audit logging, SSO options, encryption controls)

Purchase Redwood Inference through Google Cloud Marketplace to align spend with cloud procurement workflows (committed spend, invoicing, vendor onboarding), while keeping a developer-first onboarding experience.

Deployment modes
1) Hosted API (fastest start)
Use Redwood’s hosted inference API to integrate chat/text generation, embeddings, and reranking into your application.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
Reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput and data isolation controls.

3) Private (VPC / private deployment)
Private networking options for regulated workloads and tighter network controls.

NOTE: Exact availability of Dedicated/Private options via Marketplace may vary by region and contract structure. If a SKU is not visible to your billing account, contact sales for enablement.

====================================================================
4) Key benefits (bullets)
====================================================================
- Production performance: optimized serving runtime with continuous batching and caching strategies
- Flexible procurement: buy via Google Cloud Marketplace to simplify enterprise purchasing
- Deployment flexibility: consistent platform experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments
- Operational visibility: token-level latency/cost analytics and error analysis
- Reliability options: supported rollout patterns and fallback policies to reduce downtime risk

====================================================================
5) What you get (set expectations clearly)
====================================================================
What is included (typical):
- Access to Redwood Console (org management, usage analytics, model catalog)
- Entitlements corresponding to the Marketplace plan you purchase (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private and any add-ons)
- Documentation for purchase-to-provisioning steps and troubleshooting

What is NOT included by default:
- Custom model onboarding and/or bespoke performance benchmarking (may require an enterprise agreement)
- Professional services for on-prem deployments (if applicable)

====================================================================
6) Plans / SKUs (draft copy; keep high-level for listing)
====================================================================
Plans are designed to match how customers deploy and procure inference:

A) Redwood Hosted API (Usage-based)
For teams who want the fastest onboarding with usage-based billing.

B) Redwood Dedicated (Reserved capacity)
For predictable throughput and isolation needs.

C) Redwood Private (VPC / private deployment)
For regulated environments and private networking requirements.

Optional add-ons (where applicable):
- Compliance & audit add-on (additional compliance-related controls and documentation package)
- Extended observability retention add-on
- Premium SLA add-on

TODO (PM + Finance): confirm final SKU names as they must exactly match the approved SKU taxonomy; ensure consistent casing (“Hosted API”, “Dedicated”, “Private”).

====================================================================
7) How it works (simple technical explanation)
====================================================================
Redwood provides a unified inference runtime and control plane that:
- Routes requests by policy (latency/cost/region/tier)
- Optimizes execution with batching and caching
- Provides consistent APIs and operational tooling across deployment modes

For Marketplace purchases, Redwood maps your Marketplace entitlement to a Redwood organization so your engineers can start using the service quickly and your procurement team gets spend routed through Google Cloud Marketplace.

====================================================================
8) Deployment / onboarding steps (GCP Marketplace — SaaS flow)
====================================================================
Goal: make this section extremely explicit for GCP reviewers and enterprise buyers.

Prerequisites
- A Google Cloud account with access to Google Cloud Marketplace
- A billing account with permission to purchase Marketplace SaaS subscriptions
- A Redwood Inference account (can be created during activation)

Step 1 — Purchase in Google Cloud Marketplace
1. In Google Cloud Marketplace, click “Subscribe” (or “Purchase”) for the plan you want.
2. Select the appropriate Billing Account and confirm subscription.

Step 2 — Entitlement activation
After purchase, Google Cloud Marketplace creates an entitlement for your organization.
- Typical activation time: a few minutes
- In some cases (first-time vendor purchase, billing setup), activation can take longer

Step 3 — Link your Marketplace entitlement to a Redwood organization
1. Open the activation link from the Marketplace subscription page (or the “Manage on Provider” button).
2. Sign in to Redwood Console.
3. Choose one:
   a) Create a new Redwood organization (recommended for net-new customers)
   b) Link to an existing Redwood organization (recommended for expansions / moving spend)
4. Confirm linking. Your Console will show an “Entitlement: Active” state when completed.

Step 4 — Configure your deployment mode
- Hosted API:
  1) Create an API key in the Console
  2) Select your default region (if applicable)
  3) Send your first request via SDK/REST

- Dedicated / Private:
  1) After linking, your Redwood account team will coordinate capacity and networking configuration
  2) You will receive implementation steps and a mutual action plan

Step 5 — Validate end-to-end
- Make a test API call
- Confirm usage appears in Console analytics
- Confirm Marketplace subscription is visible to your procurement team

Troubleshooting quick checks
- Entitlement not active after 30–60 minutes: verify you purchased with the intended billing account; then contact support with subscription ID
- Linked to the wrong Redwood org: contact support; include the Redwood org slug + Marketplace subscription details
- Region mismatch: confirm the region selected in Redwood Console matches the plan / deployment constraints

TODO (Docs): Add link to the dedicated GCP Marketplace onboarding doc once published.

====================================================================
9) Marketplace-specific FAQs (draft)
====================================================================
Q: Is this a SaaS product or a deployment into my GCP project?
A: This is a SaaS offering purchased via Google Cloud Marketplace. Your subscription creates an entitlement that you link to your Redwood organization. No VM/image deployment into your project is required for Hosted API.

Q: How does billing work?
A: Billing for your subscription is handled through Google Cloud Marketplace. Your Redwood entitlement determines what you can use (plan + add-ons). Usage and cost analytics are also available in the Redwood Console.

Q: Can I use committed spend / invoice through Google Cloud?
A: Many customers purchase via Google Cloud Marketplace to align spend with cloud procurement workflows. Your procurement team should confirm eligibility based on your Google Cloud agreement.

Q: How do upgrades/downgrades work?
A: Plan changes are handled via Marketplace subscription changes and then reflected in Redwood entitlements. Some changes (e.g., Hosted to Dedicated/Private) may require coordination with Redwood due to capacity and configuration.

Q: What happens if I accidentally link the subscription to the wrong Redwood organization?
A: Contact Redwood Support. We can help remediate after verifying ownership of the subscription and org(s).

Q: How long does entitlement activation take?
A: Usually a few minutes. If it has been longer than 60 minutes, contact support with your Marketplace subscription details.

Q: Do you support multiple teams under one billing account?
A: Yes. Many enterprises use one billing account and multiple Redwood organizations or projects. The recommended setup depends on your security boundaries and reporting needs.

Q: Can I restrict usage to specific regions?
A: Region availability depends on your plan and deployment mode. For private deployments, networking and region constraints are configured as part of the onboarding.

Q: What support is included?
A: Support coverage depends on your plan and any premium support/SLA add-ons. For help with Marketplace activation, include your subscription ID and Redwood org in your support request.

====================================================================
10) Security, compliance, and data handling (careful wording)
====================================================================
NOTE: Keep claims consistent with the Security FAQ and what we can provide to reviewers/buyers.

Security overview
- Encryption: Data is encrypted in transit using industry-standard TLS. Encryption at rest is used for applicable stored data (details available in our security documentation).
- Access controls: Role-based access controls in the Redwood Console. SSO options may be available for enterprise plans.
- Audit logging: Redwood maintains audit logs for relevant administrative and security events (scope described in documentation).

Compliance
- Redwood maintains a security and compliance program. SOC 2 Type II reports and related evidence may be available under NDA upon request.

Data usage
- Customer prompts and outputs are processed to provide the service. Data retention and logging behavior can vary by plan and configuration.
- For regulated workloads, Redwood offers private deployment options and configurable controls (subject to plan).

Shared responsibility
- As a SaaS provider, Redwood is responsible for securing the service; customers are responsible for securing their applications, credentials, and any data they choose to send.
